Rashi on Pesachim 96b:10:1.hebrew: יקרב זה שלמים - ואע"פ שבשעת שחיטת השני, הרי הוא עומד בפנינו:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:10:1.english: This [one] shall be offered as a peace-offering - And even though at the time of the slaughter of the second [lamb], behold, it is standing before us.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:10:2.hebrew: לא שנו - דתמורה קרבה אלא שנמצא אחר שחיטה, שאפי' הפסח לא נדחה. אבל נמצא קודם שחיטה, שהוא עצמו נדחה, אע"פ שתמורתו לא נדחית בידים, אינה קריבה, שהרי מכח קדושה דחויה באה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:10:2.english: They taught - [That] the substitute may be sacrificed only when [the original lamb] was found after the slaughter [of the replacement lamb], for even the Paschal lamb [itself] was not deferred. But [if] it was found before the slaughter, when it itself was deferred, even though its substitute was not directly deferred, [the substitute] may not be sacrificed, for it comes on the strength of deferred sanctity.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:11:1.hebrew: אם כשב - הוא מקריב, גבי שלמים כתיב. "אם" יתירא הוא, דמצי למיכתב "כשב הוא מקריב". א"נ "כשב" קדריש, דהא כתיב לעיל מיניה "אם מן הצאן קרבנו", ובפרשה תחתונה אמור "ואם עז קרבנו", מכלל דעד השתא בכשב איירי, דאין לך עוד בצאן אלא כשב:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:11:1.english: If a lamb - [he] offers [it] [Leviticus 3:7]; [this] is written regarding peace-offerings. [The word] "if" is superfluous, for [Scripture] could have written: "A lamb he offers." Alternatively, it is expounding [the word] "lamb," since it is written above it: "If from the flock is his offering" [ibid. 3:6], and in the following section it is stated: "And if a goat is his offering" [ibid. 3:12] — [which implies] by deduction that until now [Scripture] is dealing with a lamb, for there is nothing else in the flock except a lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:12:1.hebrew: למה לי קרא - הא מותר הפסח הוא, ונפקא לן מוזבחת פסח דמותר הפסח אחר חצות קרב שלמים, כדאמרן באלו דברים (לעיל פסחים דף ע:), ותמורתו כ"ש דקריבה, דלא עדיפא מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:12:1.english: Why do I [need] a verse - This is a leftover Paschal offering, and we derive from "you shall slaughter the Paschal offering" that a leftover Paschal offering after midday is offered as a peace-offering, as we said in [the chapter] Eilu Devarim (above, Pesachim 70b), and its substitute is all the more so offered, for it is no better than it.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:12:2.hebrew: והמיר בו אחר שחיטה - ואשמעינן דאע"ג דאיהו לא קרב, תמורתו קריבה, הואיל ולא הוקדשה קודם שחיטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:12:2.english: And he substituted for it after the slaughter - And [it] teaches us that even though [the original animal] itself is not offered, its substitute is offered, since it was not consecrated before the slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:14:1.hebrew: כשב - קרא יתירא כדפרישית, מדכתיב בתריה ואם עז, מכלל דעד השתא בכשב איירי:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:14:1.english: Lamb - [This is] a superfluous verse, as I explained [earlier]; since it is written after it, "And if [his offering be] a goat," [it follows] by implication that until now [Scripture] was speaking of a lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:14:2.hebrew: לאליה - דבכל קרבנות כשב, אליה כתיבא עם האימורין. בשלמים — חלבו האליה (ויקרא ג), ובאשם כתיב (שם ז) את כל חלבו ירים ממנו את האליה וגו', וחטאת כאשם. אבל פסח, אימורין גופייהו לא כתיבי בהדיא, אלא כדנפקא לן (לעיל פסחים דף סד:) מאת דמם תזרוק ואת חלבם תקטיר. הלכך, אלייתו צריכה להתרבות בקרבנות, שבשור לא הוזכרה אליה באימוריו:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:14:2.english: For the fat tail - For in all offerings of a lamb, the fat tail is written together with the sacrificial parts. In [the case of] a peace-offering, [it states:] "its fat, the fat tail" (Leviticus 3); and in [the case of] a guilt-offering, it is written (ibid. 7): "all its fat he shall offer up from it, the fat tail, etc."; and a sin-offering [is] like a guilt-offering. However, [regarding] the Paschal lamb, the sacrificial parts themselves are not written explicitly, rather [they are known] as we derive [them] (above, Pesachim 64b) from: "their blood you shall dash, and their fat you shall burn." Therefore, its fat tail needs to be included [explicitly] among the offerings, because in [the case of] an ox, the fat tail was not mentioned among its sacrificial parts.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:15:1.hebrew: ושלמים הבאין מחמת פסח - מותר פסח, כגון תמורתו ופסח שנתכפרו בעליו באחר. כך שמעתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:15:1.english: And peace-offerings that come due to a Paschal lamb - [This refers to] the remainder of a Paschal lamb, such as its substitute or a Paschal lamb whose owners attained atonement through another [Paschal lamb]. So I have heard.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:15:2.hebrew: לכל מצות - מצות שלמים גרסינן, שיהא דין כל חומר שלמים עליהן. לשון אחר: הבאין מחמת פסח — חגיגת ארבעה עשר. וזו שמעתי [וכך קבל רבי]:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:15:2.english: In all the mitzvot [of] - We read [the text as] "mitzvot of peace-offerings," [meaning] that the law of every stringency of peace-offerings applies to them. Another explanation: "[Peace-offerings] that come due to a Paschal lamb" [refers to] the festival offering [chagigah] of the fourteenth [of Nisan]. And this is what I heard [and thus my teacher received].

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:16:1.hebrew: ואם - הפסק הוא, להפסיק בין כשב לעז, שבכשב נתפרשה אליה, כדכתיב "האליה תמימה לעומת העצה" — ממקום שהכליות יועצות — ובא הכתוב והפסיק ולמד על העז שאינה טעונה אליה, להקריב אליה שלה למזבח. יש מפרשין: עז אין לו אליה; וטעות הוא בידם, שהרי ממקום שהכליות יועצות היא ניטלית, ועוד: מה לימד הכתוב הואיל ואין לו:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:16:1.english: And if - It is an interruption, to separate between a lamb and a she-goat; for regarding a lamb, the fat tail was explicitly stated, as it is written: "the whole fat tail close to the backbone" — [meaning] from the place where the kidneys give counsel — and Scripture came and interrupted [the subject], and taught regarding the she-goat that it does not require a fat tail, [that is,] to offer its fat tail upon the altar. Some explain [that] a she-goat has no fat tail; but this is an error in their hands, for it is removed from the place where the kidneys give counsel, and furthermore: what did Scripture teach [by excluding it], since it has none?

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:17:1.english: Some teach - [It refers] to this [statement of] "they only taught" of Rabbah.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:18:1.hebrew: לא שנו - שאף תמורתו דחויה, אלא שנמצא קודם שחיטה והמיר בו קודם שחיטה, דכי שחטיה דחינהו לתרוייהו הני, שהיו ראויין ועומדים לפסח ונקבעו:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:18:1.english: They taught only - that even its substitute is rejected, except where [the original lamb] was found before the slaughter and one performed substitution with it before the slaughter; for when he slaughtered [the replacement], it rejected both of these, which were fit and standing [ready] for the Paschal offering, and they became established [as rejected].

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:18:2.hebrew: אבל המיר בו אחר שחיטה - אע"פ שהפסח רועה, התמורה קריבה, שהרי לא נדחית:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:18:2.english: But [if] he performed substitution with it after slaughter - Even though the Paschal lamb is left to graze, the substitute is offered [as a peace-offering], for it was not rejected.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:18:3.english: Something that is not fit for it - For it had not yet been consecrated.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:1:1.hebrew: ואלא אחמץ - דאיסור חימוצו נוהג כל שבעה. מכלל דלילה אחד דקתני מתני' בפסח מצרים אחמץ קאי, וה"ק: ואין חימוצו נוהג אלא לילה אחד, ופסח דורות נוהג כל שבעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:1:1.english: Rather, [it refers] to leavened bread - whose prohibition of leavening applies all seven [days]. [This implies] by inference that "one night," which the Mishnah teaches regarding the Passover of Egypt, refers to leavened bread, and this is what it is saying: its [prohibition of] leavening applies only for one night, whereas [for] the Passover of generations it applies all seven [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:1:2.english: One day - [This] implies the entire day.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:1:3.english: No leavened bread shall be eaten; this day - And juxtaposed to it [is the verse]: "This day you go forth."

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:2:1.hebrew: אלא - הכי משמע: ונאכל בחפזון בלילה אחד, וה"ה דפסח דורות נמי לילה אחד, ופסח מצרים חימוצו נוהג כל היום, ופסח דורות כל שבעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:2:1.english: Rather - This is what it means: and it is eaten in haste on one night, and the same law applies to the Paschal lamb of [later] generations as well, [that it is eaten for] one night; and [regarding] the Passover of Egypt, its [prohibition of] leavened bread applies the entire day, and [regarding] the Passover of [later] generations, [it applies] all seven [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:3:2.english: That the substitute of the Paschal offering is sacrificed - [As] a peace-offering after Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:3:3.hebrew: ותמורת הפסח אינה קריבה - ויש תמורת פסח שאינה קריבה היא עצמה שלמים, אלא רועה עד שיסתאב במום ותמכר, ויביא בדמיה שלמים, דמותר הפסח קרב שלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:3:3.english: And the substitute of the Paschal lamb is not sacrificed - And there is a substitute of a Paschal lamb that is not itself sacrificed as a peace-offering; rather, it grazes until it becomes disqualified by a blemish and is sold, and one brings a peace-offering with its proceeds, for a leftover Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:3:4.hebrew: ואין לי לפרש - שכחתי על איזה שמעתי תקרב, ועל איזה שמעתי תרעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:3:4.english: And I cannot explain - I forgot regarding which [case] I heard "it shall be offered," and regarding which [case] I heard "it shall graze."

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:4:1.hebrew: הפסח - שאבד והפריש אחר תחתיו, ונמצא הראשון קודם שחיטת השני — דהיה עומד לפנינו בשעת שחיטה, הרי קבעתו שעת שחיטה בשם פסח, וזה שלא הקריבו, דחהו בידים. לא יקרב עוד הוא עצמו שלמים, דאין זה מותר הפסח אלא פסח [דחוי]:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:4:1.english: The Paschal lamb - That was lost, and he separated another in its stead, and the first was found before the slaughter of the second — since it was standing before us at the time of slaughter, the time of slaughter established it with the designation of a Paschal lamb, and [by] not sacrificing it, he actively rejected it. It itself shall no longer be offered [as] a peace-offering, for this is not a leftover Paschal lamb, rather a [rejected] Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:4:2.hebrew: וכן תמורתו - אם המיר הוא בו בהמת חולין אחרי כן, הרי הוא כמוהו — אין קרב הוא עצמו שלמים, אלא דמיו. ואם לאחר שחיטת השני נמצא, הרי לא קבעתו שעת שחיטה בשם פסח ולא נדחה בידים, ויביא שלמים, ויקרב הוא עצמו שלמים. וה"ה דמצי למיתני "רבי יהושע אומר: פסח קרב ופסח אינו קרב", ובגמרא פריך לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:4:2.english: And so too, its substitute - If he substituted a non-sacred animal for it afterward, it is like it — it itself is not offered as a peace-offering, rather [only] its proceeds [are used]. And if it is found after the slaughter of the second [lamb], then the time of slaughter did not establish it with the designation of a Paschal offering, nor was it actively rejected; [thus] he brings a peace-offering, and it itself is offered as a peace-offering. And by the same token, [the Tanna] could have taught: "Rabbi Yehoshua says: A Paschal lamb is offered and a Paschal lamb is not offered," and in the Gemara it raises this question.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:6:1.hebrew: דאיכא תמורת הפסח דלא קרבה - ולא אמרינן מתחלה שלמים היא, ואפילו המיר קודם שחיטה, לא קבעתה זמן השחיטה בשם פסח ואין בה דחוי, אלא אף היא נקבעת בפסח ונדחת:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:6:1.english: That there is a substitute [for] the Paschal offering that is not sacrificed - And we do not say [that] from the outset it is a peace-offering, and [that] even if he substituted [it] before [the time of] slaughter, the time of slaughter did not establish it with the designation of a Paschal offering and it is not subject to rejection; rather, it too is established as a Paschal offering and is rejected.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:7:1.hebrew: קודם שחיטה ואחר שחיטה - דוקא שנינו במשנתנו, ולא שנינו בה זמן שחיטה, דהיינו חצות. ואשמעינן, דאפילו היה אבוד בשעת חצות, אם נמצא קודם שחיטת השני, הוא נקבע ונדחה, הואיל ונדחה להקריבו לפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:7:1.english: Before slaughter and after slaughter - We learned [this] specifically in our Mishnah, and we did not learn in it the time of slaughter, which is midday. And it teaches us that even if it was lost at the time of midday, if it was found before the slaughter of the second [lamb], it becomes established [as a Paschal offering] and rejected, since it was rejected [from] offering it as a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:7:2.hebrew: קודם חצות שנינו - שעת חצות היא הקובעתו בפסח. אם נמצא קודם חצות, קבעתיה חצות, שהרי נראה, וכי לא אקרביה, דחייה. אבל נמצא אחר חצות, אפי' נמצא קודם שחיטה, אין כאן קביעות ולא דחוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 96b:7:2.english: We learned: Before midday - The hour of midday is what establishes it as a Pesach [offering]. If it was found before midday, midday established it, for it was fit [to be offered], and when he did not offer it, he rejected it. However, [if] it was found after midday, even [if] it was found before the slaughter [of the replacement], there is neither establishment nor rejection here.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:9:1.english: Before the slaughter - Of the second [one].

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:9:2.english: Before midday - And he achieved atonement through another [animal], it shall graze.

Rashi on Pesachim 96b:9:3.english: After midday - And he achieved atonement with another [animal].

Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:15:1.hebrew: ושלמים הבאין מחמת הפסח - לפי אותו לשון דפירש בקונטרס דהנך שלמים היינו חגיגת י"ד, אין לחוש מה (שפירש) באלו דברים (דף ע"א: ד"ה לימד) דשלמים הבאים מחמת פסח בפרק כל הפסולים (זבחים דף לו.) היינו מותר פסח, דהא כדאיתא והא כדאיתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:15:1.english: And peace-offerings that come due to the Paschal lamb - According to that version that Rashi explained, that these peace-offerings are the festival-offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan], there is no need to be concerned about what (he explained) in [chapter] Eilu Devarim (71b, s.v. limmed) that "peace-offerings that come due to a Paschal lamb" in chapter Kol HaPesulim (Zevachim 36a) means the remainder of a Paschal lamb, for this [one] is as it is and that [one] is as it is.

Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:16:1.hebrew: ואם עז הפסיק הענין - פירש ריב"א: מדלא כלל אותו בהדי כבש, אלא הפסיק הענין וכתבו לבדו, ולא שינה בו כלום אלא דלא כתיב ביה אליה — להכי כתביה למעוטי מתורת אליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:16:1.english: "And if [his offering is] a she-goat" — it interrupted the matter - Riva explained: Since [Scripture] did not include it together with the lamb, but rather interrupted the matter and wrote it by itself, and did not change anything in it except that "fat tail" is not written in it — therefore [Scripture] wrote it [separately] to exclude [the she-goat] from the law of the fat tail.

Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:2:1.hebrew: נאכל בחפזון לילה אחד וה"ה לפסח דורות - ואם תאמר: א"כ אמאי תנייה כלל במתניתין, כיון דשוים בזה? ויש לומר: דתנייה אגב דבעי למיתני "וחמוצו כל היום ופסח דורות נוהג כל שבעה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:2:1.english: [It was] eaten in haste [for] one night, and the same applies to the Paschal lamb of [later] generations - And if you ask: If so, why did [the Tanna] teach it in the Mishnah at all, since they are equal in this [respect]? One can answer: [He] taught it incidentally, because he wanted to teach, "and its [prohibition against] leavened bread [applied] the entire day, and [on] Passover [in later] generations it applies all seven [days]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:4:1.hebrew: קודם שחיטת הפסח ירעה - וטעמא דדחייה בידים, כדפירש רש"י. ואפי' רב דאמר אין בעלי חיים נדחין ופליג אר' יוחנן בפ' שני שעירי (יומא דף סד.) — היינו דוקא כגון דלא דחייה בידים, כגון נטמאו בעלים או שמשכו ידיהם. וא"ת: והא משמע דפליג בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ז.), דא"ר יוחנן: בהמה של ב' שותפין, הקדיש חציה וחזר ולקחה והקדיש חציה — קדושה ואינה קריבה, משום דנדחת בתחלה כשהקדיש חציה, ודייק עלה: ש"מ בעלי חיים נדחין; משמע דרב פליג. וי"ל: כיון דדרך הקדש דחי לה, לא מיקרי כל כך דחוי בידים. ובתוספתא [פ"ט] פליגי רבי יוסי ורבנן איזה מהן יקריב לכתחלה, ומייתי לה בפ' שני שעירי (יומא דף סד.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:4:1.english: Before the slaughter of the Paschal lamb, it shall graze - And the reason is that he actively pushed it aside, as Rashi explained. And even Rav, who says that living animals do not become permanently disqualified and disagrees with Rabbi Yochanan in the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei (Yoma 64a) — that is specifically where he did not actively push it aside, such as [when] the owners became impure or withdrew their hands [from the offering]. And if you ask: But it implies that [Rav] disagrees in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a), where Rabbi Yochanan said: [Regarding] an animal belonging to two partners, [if one] consecrated half of it, and then went back and bought [the other half] and consecrated half of it, it is consecrated but cannot be offered, because it was pushed aside at the outset when he consecrated half of it; and [the Gemara] infers from this: "Conclude from this that living animals become permanently disqualified" — which implies that Rav disagrees. And one can answer: Since he pushes it aside through the manner of consecration, it is not considered so much an active rejection. And in the Tosefta [ch. 9], Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis disagree as to which of them one should offer initially, and [the Gemara] cites it in the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei (Yoma 64a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:6:1.hebrew: קמ"ל דאיכא תמורת הפסח דלא קרבה - דקבע לה חצות או שחיטה, דס"ד דלא קבע הואיל ובאיסור הוקדשה ואין דעתו עליה לשוחטה לשם פסח, קמ"ל דאפילו הכי קבע לה. ור"י מפרש דס"ד הואיל ואינה קריבה לעולם לשם פסח, מתחלתה שלמים היא; קמ"ל. ומתוך פרש"י דפי': "אלא אף היא נקבעת בפסח ונדחה", משמע שסובר שלפי האמת ראויה לפסח:
Tosafot on Pesachim 96b:6:1.english: [This] teaches us that there is a substitute for the Paschal lamb that is not sacrificed - For midday or [the time of] slaughter establishes it [as a Paschal offering], as it might have entered your mind that it does not establish [it], since it was consecrated in prohibition and his intention is not upon it to slaughter it for the sake of a Paschal offering; [therefore, the Gemara] teaches us that even so, it establishes it. And R. Yitzchak explains that it might have entered your mind [to say] that since it is never offered for the sake of a Paschal offering, it is a peace-offering from the outset; [therefore, the Gemara] teaches us [otherwise]. And from Rashi's commentary, who explained: "Rather, it too is established as a Paschal offering and becomes rejected," it is implied that he holds that in truth it is fit for a Paschal offering.
